narrative.overview:
Eigentone is a precision instrument the listener owns: a graphite enamel faceplate, ivory that lights up, engraved condensed legends, a fine graph grid and readouts that hold still. Screens are dense because their users know Q and dB, and because a visit is short and happens with music playing.

Colour always carries meaning. Blue and red belong to the left and right ear, as on an audiogram, and every per-ear graph marks the left with X and the right with O. The system refuses the category's glossy dark app with coloured pill sliders and rounded cards.

Six decisions came directly from the user and override the original direction contract. They are binding: no horizontal scrolling; preset switching by dropdown under the app name; a deep green status strip; effects in the strip with a drawn tick or cross; bars darker than the page with no scroll fades; ivory filter points on graphs.

**Known limits:** Dark theme only. No authored motion beyond the playing pulse; anything else that moves is stock Material behaviour. Left and right are only partly mirrored, in graph legends and curves. Tool and test screens (hearing check, sweep, peak finder, Find my sound, A/B compare, shape browser) inherit these tokens but were not redesigned. No tablet layout: content is simply capped at 640dp and centred.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite surfaces separated by tone, with no shadows on panels or keys
Ivory for what is lit, active or grippable; ear colours only for the ears
Barlow Semi Condensed legends, Barlow body, JetBrains Mono digits
Rectangular fader caps with a centre line, on thin rails with engraved scales
Everything fits the width: wrap or drop down, never scroll sideways

rules.name: The Ear Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue and red mean left and right ear, and nothing else. Any other second state uses ivory, dim text or a shape.

rules.name: The Ivory Rule
rules.body: Ivory means lit, active, or a handle you can grip. Plain text stays Text, including text buttons and the app name, so that ivory keeps its meaning. Filter points are ivory because they apply to both ears (user decision).

rules.name: The Green Strip Rule
rules.body: Green is the one exception to "the ears are the only chroma" besides Danger Orange, and it belongs to the status strip alone (user decision). Do not reuse it for accents, and keep the band's hue clear of the ear colours.

rules.name: The Still Digits Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes while you watch it is set in JetBrains Mono, so that it does not shift as its value changes.

rules.name: The Engraved Legend Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked type is only the heading of a group of rows. It never sits above another heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The No Sideways Rule
rules.body: Nothing scrolls horizontally, anywhere. Short sets wrap with `FlowRow` (8dp gaps), and long lists use dropdowns (user decision).

rules.name: The Tonal Ladder Rule
rules.body: Surface height is shown by tone. A pressed unlit key becomes Enamel, and a pressed lit key becomes Pressed Ivory.

rules.name: The Fixed Bars Rule
rules.body: Top and bottom bars are darker than the page, with no scroll fades or gradients (user decision). The step is deliberately quiet (1.07:1), so the strip (1.67:1 against the page) marks the top edge.

rules.name: The Drawn State Rule
rules.body: On and off are shown by a drawn mark as well as a colour, and each tag is announced with its state.

rules.name: The True Reading Rule
rules.body: Nothing is drawn as a live measurement unless it is one. The compressor shows as on rather than with a meter, because Android does not report gain reduction.

dos: Do use `Palette`, `KeyShape`, `PanelShape` and the type styles in `Theme.kt` rather than new literals.
Do draw right-ear lines dashed and mark ears with X and O wherever a graph is per-ear.
Do set changing numbers in Readout, in ivory when they differ from the default and Dim Text when they do not.
Do give every graph or fader gesture a button or slider alternative for screen readers.
Do keep the deep green strip as the only green surface, with drawn ticks and crosses for effects.
Do wrap short sets and put long lists in dropdowns.
donts: Don't use blue or red for anything except the ears, or use red for errors.
Don't use ear colours for filter points; they apply to both ears.
Don't add scroll fades or gradients to the bars.
Don't bring back the rejected purple strip, or a row of preset keys in the first viewport.
Don't add coloured pill sliders, rounded cards or shadows on panels and keys.
Don't draw an invented meter or present an estimate as a measurement.
